===============================================================================

COURSE OVERVIEW:
Course Code: CS301
Course Name: Database Management Systems (DBMS)
Credits: 4
Prerequisites: Data Structures (CS202)
Instructor: Dr. Robert Edgar (Email: r.edgar@college.edu, Office: Tech-402)

UNIT 1: INTRODUCTION & DATABASE ARCHITECTURE
- Fundamental concepts: Data, Database, DBMS, Data Independence (Physical & Logical).
- Database Architecture: 3-Schema Architecture (Internal, Conceptual, External).
- Data Models: Relational, ER Diagram, Entity Types, Relationship Sets, Weak Entities, Keys (Primary, Candidate, Foreign, Super Key).

UNIT 2: RELATIONAL ALGEBRA & SQL
- Relational Algebra Operations: Select, Project, Union, Set Difference, Cartesian Product, Join (Inner, Outer, Equi-join).
- Structured Query Language (SQL): DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP), DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), DQL (SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY).
- Advanced SQL: Subqueries, Correlated Subqueries, Views, Triggers, Indexes.

UNIT 3: NORMALIZATION & DATABASE DESIGN (IMPORTANT TOPICS)
- Relational Database Design & Functional Dependencies (FDs).
- Closure of Functional Dependencies & Attribute Closure Algorithm.
- Normal Forms: 1NF (First Normal Form), 2NF (Second Normal Form), 3NF (Third Normal Form), BCNF (Boyce-Codd Normal Form).
- Important Topics for Exams: Decompositions, Lossless Join Property, Dependency Preservation, BCNF vs 3NF trade-offs.

UNIT 4: TRANSACTION PROCESSING & CONCURRENCY CONTROL
- Transaction Concepts: ACID Properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability).
- Transaction States: Active, Partially Committed, Committed, Failed, Aborted.
- Concurrency Control Techniques: Lock-based Protocols (2PL - Two Phase Locking), Deadlock Handling (Prevention, Detection, Recovery), Timestamp Ordering Protocol.

UNIT 5: RECOVERY SYSTEMS & STORAGE ARCHITECTURE
- Storage Structures: File Organization, Indexing Structures (B-Trees, B+ Trees, Hashing).
- Recovery Systems: Log-Based Recovery, Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), Checkpoints, Shadow Paging.

LAPLACE TRANSFORMS 
Introduction  
         Laplace Transformations were introduced by Pierre Simmon Marquis De Laplace (1749-
1827), a French Mathematician known as a Newton of French. Laplace Transformations is a 
powerful technique; it replaces operations of calculus by operations of algebra. An Ordinary (or) 
Partial Differential Equation together with Initial conditions is reduced to a problem of solving 
an Algebraic Equation by this method.  
 
       Laplace transform is a very powerful mathematical tool applied in various areas of 
engineering and science. With the increasing complexity of engineering problems, Laplace 
transforms help in solving complex problems with a very simple approach just like the 
applications of transfer functions to solve ordinary differential equations.Laplace Transform 
methods have a key role to play in the modern approach to the analysis and design of engineering 
system.The purpose of the Laplace Transform is to transform ordinary differential equations 
(ODEs) into algebraic equations, which can then be solved by the formal rules of algebra. This 
makes it easier to solve ODEs. The concepts of Laplace Transforms are applied in the area of 
science and technology such as Electrical engineering, Communication engineering, Mechanical 
engineering ,Computer engineering,Control engineering, Civil engineering and Nuclear physics 
etc.  
     Laplace Transform is widely used by electronic engineers to solve quickly differential 
equations occurring in the analysis of electronic circuits,Digital signal processing, System 
modeling, Process   Control. In Mechanical engineering field Laplace Transform is widely used to 
solve differential equations occurring in mathematical modeling of mechanical system to find 
transfer function of that particular system. In Computer scienceengineering it is used in Data 
mining (which is the analysis step of Knowledge Discovery in Databases) which focuses on the 
discovery of (previously) unknown properties on the data, where Laplace equation is used to 
determine the prediction and analyses the step of knowledge in databases.Laplace Transformations 
helps to find out the current and some criteria for the analyzing the circuits. It is used to build 
required ICs and chips for systems.So it plays a vital role in field of computer science. In order to 
get the true form of radioactive decay a Laplace Transform is used in Nuclear Physics .In Civil 
engineering it can be applied to analyze behavior of complex systems, such as bridges, 
skyscrapers, and so forth.In Aeronautical engineering Laplace transform is a valuable “tool” in 
solving Differential equations in “feedback control” systems for example, in stability and control 
of aircraft systems.

NARASARAOPETA ENGINEERING COLLEGE (AUTONOMOUS) - B.TECH CSE / AI-ML / DATA SCIENCE SYLLABUS
===============================================================================
Source URL: https://www.nrtec.in/syllabus-2/
Regulation: R20 / R23 Autonomous Curriculum
Branches: Computer Science & Engineering (CSE), AI & Machine Learning (CSE-AI/ML), Data Science (CSE-DS)

COURSE 1: CS201 - DATA STRUCTURES & ALGORITHMS
- Unit 1: Stacks, Queues, Circular Queues, Priority Queues, Infix to Postfix Conversion.
- Unit 2: Linked Lists (Singly, Doubly, Circular), Dynamic Memory Allocation.
- Unit 3: Trees & Binary Search Trees (BST), AVL Trees, Red-Black Trees, Heap Sort.
- Unit 4: Graph Algorithms: BFS, DFS, Dijkstra Shortest Path, Prim's & Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree.
- Unit 5: Searching & Sorting: Bubble, Selection, Insertion, Quick Sort, Merge Sort, Hashing Techniques.

COURSE 2: CS302 - OPERATING SYSTEMS (OS)
- Unit 1: OS Structures, System Calls, Process Management, Process Control Block (PCB), CPU Scheduling Algorithms (FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, Priority).
- Unit 2: Process Synchronization: Critical Section Problem, Semaphores, Monitors, Classical IPC Problems (Producer-Consumer, Dining Philosophers).
- Unit 3: Deadlocks: Characterization, Prevention, Avoidance (Banker's Algorithm), Detection & Recovery.
- Unit 4: Memory Management: Paging, Segmentation, Virtual Memory, Demand Paging, Page Replacement Algorithms (FIFO, LRU, Optimal).
- Unit 5: File Systems: Directory Implementation, Allocation Methods (Contiguous, Linked, Indexed), Disk Scheduling (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN).

COURSE 3: CS303 - COMPUTER NETWORKS (CN)
- Unit 1: OSI Reference Model vs TCP/IP Protocol Suite, Physical Layer, Guided & Unguided Transmission Media.
- Unit 2: Data Link Layer: Framing, Error Detection & Correction (CRC, Hamming Code), Sliding Window Protocols (Stop-and-Wait, Go-Back-N, Selective Repeat).
- Unit 3: Network Layer: IPv4 & IPv6 Addressing, Subnetting, Routing Algorithms (Distance Vector, Link State Routing - OSPF, BGP).
- Unit 4: Transport Layer: TCP Connection Management, 3-Way Handshake, Flow Control, Congestion Control (TCP Tahoe, Reno), UDP.
- Unit 5: Application Layer: DNS, HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, DHCP, Network Security Fundamentals.

COURSE 4: CS401 - ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE & MACHINE LEARNING (AI/ML)
- Unit 1: Problem Formulation, Uninformed Search (BFS, DFS) & Informed Search (A* Search, Heuristic Functions).
- Unit 2: Knowledge Representation, First-Order Logic, Inference, Resolution, Expert Systems.
- Unit 3: Supervised Learning: Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines (SVM).
- Unit 4: Unsupervised Learning & Clustering: K-Means, Hierarchical Clustering, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) Dimensionality Reduction.
- Unit 5: Deep Learning & Neural Networks: Perceptrons, Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP), Backpropagation, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN).

COURSE 5: CS402 - WEB TECHNOLOGIES & FULL-STACK DEVELOPMENT
- Unit 1: HTML5, CSS3, Responsive Web Design, Flexbox, Grid, JavaScript Syntax, DOM Manipulation, ES6 Features.
- Unit 2: React.js Fundamentals: Components, JSX, State & Props, Hooks (useState, useEffect), Event Handling.
- Unit 3: Backend REST API Design: Node.js, Express.js Framework, Routing, Middleware, Authentication (JWT).
- Unit 4: Database Integration: MongoDB / PostgreSQL, Mongoose ORM, Async/Await Data Pipelines.
- Unit 5: Software Engineering & DevOps: Git/GitHub Version Control, CI/CD Pipelines, Docker Containers, Cloud Deployment.

COURSE 1: EC201 - SIGNALS & SYSTEMS & DIGITAL SIGNAL PROCESSING (DSP)
- Unit 1: Continuous-Time & Discrete-Time Signals, LTI Systems, Convolution, Fourier Series & Fourier Transforms.
- Unit 2: Z-Transforms, ROC Properties, Inverse Z-Transform, System Function H(z).
- Unit 3: Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) Decimation-in-Time (DIT) & Decimation-in-Frequency (DIF).
- Unit 4: IIR Filter Design: Butterworth & Chebyshev Filters, Impulse Invariance & Bilinear Transformations.
- Unit 5: FIR Filter Design: Windowing Techniques (Rectangular, Hamming, Hanning, Blackman), Linear Phase FIR Filters.

COURSE 2: EC301 - VLSI DESIGN & EMBEDDED SYSTEMS
- Unit 1: MOS Transistor Theory, CMOS Fabrication Process, NMOS, PMOS, CMOS Inverter DC Characteristics.
- Unit 2: Layout Design Rules, Stick Diagrams, Pass Transistor Logic, Transmission Gates.
- Unit 3: Microcontrollers: 8051 & ARM Cortex Architecture, Registers, Interrupts, Timers, Serial Communication (UART, SPI, I2C).
